comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
RE-TYPED bug -> story and left OPEN and UNCLAIMED for a dedicated implementer. Not abandoned: the plan in the description is the current, four-times-reviewed design and is the right starting point.

WHY. This began as a follow-up split out of silvern-dewy-damselfly's plan review — 'make the closed-without-signature state detectable by a later reader'. Four plan reviews grew it well past bug-follow-up size, and each round was legitimate discovery rather than wording:

R1 BLOCK — a single boolean cannot express the multi-way discriminator the ACs demand, and the plan never said how 'a signature was expected' is computed or threaded (it is NOT verified_result, which is None for a --force close even though a signature WAS expected).
R2 BLOCK — the enum omitted the DISPOSITION close, a genuinely distinct expectation that _completion_precheck already produces (close_precheck.py:441-446) and that would otherwise misread as a verified completion; and it omitted the config-unreadable fail-open, where recording gate_off would launder a FAULT into a policy choice. Also: AC2 requires reading from reduced state, so the reducer fold and ticket_state schema had to join the edit set.
R3 BLOCK (new scope, which is why this stops here) — two structural findings the earlier rounds had not reached. gate_enabled (gates.py:79-87) returns a bare bool that is False for BOTH gate-off and config-unreadable, so it COLLAPSES the two before _completion_precheck can observe the difference: the enum cannot be produced without changing that function's signature, a new edit site the plan does not own. And idea->closed never enters _completion_precheck at all (close_ticket guards the call with current_status != 'idea'), so not_applicable has no named computation site.

WHERE IT STANDS. The current description carries: an 8-value completion_expectation enum recorded on the close STATUS event in the same locked write as the close (no extra lock — which is the whole point, since an audit comment or second event would append through the very lock whose timeout causes the failure being recorded); a derivation table combining the durable expectation with the durable attestation; and the close_class precedent for event-write + fold-at-both-*->closed-edges + reduced-state schema.

WHAT THE NEXT IMPLEMENTER MUST RESOLVE FIRST (the R3 findings):
1. gate_enabled must distinguish gate-off from config-unreadable, or the expectation must be computed somewhere that can see the difference. Its current fail-open bool is the blocker.
2. Name an owner for not_applicable, since idea->closed bypasses _completion_precheck entirely.
3. Add ACs exercising gate_unreadable and disposition — R3 correctly noted both carry distinct semantics with no criterion asserting them.

NOT BLOCKING ANYTHING SHIPPED. silvern-dewy-damselfly (change 1673) makes the loss machine-readable to the caller that suffered it across library, CLI and MCP, and is independent of this. This ticket is only about an unrelated LATER reader.

Related: defiant-orthoclase-buck (055d-f176-8fcb-4ffe) touches the same STATUS event with a much smaller change and should be sequenced with this, not merged into it.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Operator decision (2026-08-19): NO new epic. This stays a STORY, and R3's first blocker has been
split out as its own ticket which now BLOCKS this one.

Reasoning: wolverine's pieces all serve ONE outcome — a later reader can tell the close states apart
— which is a story with prerequisites, not an epic with independent value streams. An epic would add
ceremony without buying sequencing that a blocking link does not already give.

R3 blocker 1 is now `steep-tired-whimbrel` (f5c4-b2d1-4503-4bfe) — "gate_enabled fails OPEN and
collapses gate-off with config-unreadable". It was filed separately because the defect stands on its
own merit: an unreadable config silently DISABLES the completion-verification gate and is
indistinguishable from a deliberate gate-off, so a fault is laundered into a policy choice. That is
worth fixing whether or not this ticket is ever built. Resolution approach recorded there: tri-state
at the SOURCE, failing CLOSED on unreadable — not recomputing the distinction at call sites, which
would be a second config read that drifts.

R3 blocker 2 (owner for `not_applicable`, since idea->closed bypasses _completion_precheck entirely)
is a DECISION, not a ticket. Operator direction: set it explicitly on the `idea -> closed` transition
path, which is the only place that knows the gate never applied.

R3 blocker 3 (ACs for `gate_unreadable` and `disposition`) is deliberately DEFERRED until
steep-tired-whimbrel lands. Authoring those criteria now would be guessing at an enum whose shape is
not yet settled — which is how the previous four review rounds each discovered new scope.

Coordination note: RP-06 (`uneducated-habitual-primate`) should CONSUME the tri-state rather than
build its own. This was deliberately not folded into RP-06 so a small independently-landable fix is
not coupled to a large program's schedule.

comments.body: OPERATOR RULING (2026-08-21): option (a) APPROVED — persist close provenance durably. Record the gate-state/close-provenance in the close STATUS event itself (event-schema addition) so a later reader can distinguish: gate-off close, --force close (with its reason — note txn.transition_core currently discards force_close_reason, tracked separately under defiant-orthoclase-buck; coordinate, don't duplicate), local unattested close, certifiable-false withholding, and signature-append failure. The audit sidecar remains an audit surface, not the discriminator. Implementation must follow docs/event-schema.md and docs/migrations.md (additive, reducer-known, backward-compatible with historical events that lack the field).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Coordination check per the operator ruling: defiant-orthoclase-buck (055d-f176-8fcb-4ffe) is CLOSED — the txn.transition_core force_close_reason discard was already fixed by change 1680 (commit 6cb803c918): the reason is now written present-only onto the *->closed STATUS event and folded into reduced state. Nothing to fix there in this ticket; completion_expectation=force_bypassed will sit NEXT TO that already-durable force_close_reason, same event, same locked write. steep-tired-whimbrel (f5c4-b2d1-4503-4bfe) also CLOSED — gates.gate_enabled returns the tri-state GateState, which this plan consumes for gate_off vs gate_unreadable. Description rewritten to a template-conformant plan incorporating the ruling and the resolved R3 blockers (not_applicable owner = the idea->closed path in close_ticket; ACs added for gate_unreadable and disposition).

compiled_state.description:
Split from silvern-dewy-damselfly (f4cf-60b2-41c0-4843). OPERATOR RULING (2026-08-21, latest
comment): option (a) approved — persist close provenance durably in the close STATUS event.

## Context / Problem

After a close whose completion-signature append failed, a later reader cannot tell that
ticket apart from one closed with the gate off (damselfly reports the loss only in the
returned payload — ephemeral). The gate's state at close time is read from config and
discarded (`_completion_precheck`, `_commands/close_precheck.py`), so "closed with no
attestation" collapses into ONE state: gate off, `--force` close, config-unreadable
fail-open, `source == "local"` unattested close, `certifiable is False` withholding, and
signature-append failure.

Landed prerequisites:

* steep-tired-whimbrel (f5c4-b2d1-4503-4bfe, CLOSED) — `gates.gate_enabled` returns the
  tri-state `GateState` (ENABLED / DISABLED / UNREADABLE); this plan CONSUMES it, never
  recomputes it.
* defiant-orthoclase-buck (055d-f176-8fcb-4ffe, CLOSED) — `force_close_reason` is persisted
  on the close STATUS event and folded; `force_bypassed` complements that durable reason.
* Owner for `not_applicable` (operator decision): set explicitly on the `idea -> closed`
  path in `transition_close.close_ticket`, which alone knows the gate never applied.

## Approach

Record on the `*->closed` STATUS event WHY a completion signature was or was not expected —
in the SAME locked write that commits the close (`txn.transition_core`), so NO additional
lock acquisition (an audit comment or second event would append through the very write-lock
whose timeout causes the failure being recorded).

`completion_expectation` is a present-only string ENUM (a bool cannot separate the states
the ACs demand), total over the close path:

| value | meaning at close time |
|---|---|
| `required` | the gate ran; a completion signature was expected |
| `disposition` | a qualifying administrative close: signed as a DISPOSITION, not a PASS |
| `gate_off` | a readable config had the gate off (DISABLED — a policy choice) |
| `gate_unreadable` | unreadable config, gate failed OPEN (UNREADABLE — a FAULT, not laundered into `gate_off`) |
| `force_bypassed` | the gate was ENABLED and `--force` skipped it (its reason is the sibling `force_close_reason`) |
| `local_source` | verdict `source == "local"`: verified but never signed |
| `not_certifiable` | `certifiable is False`: certification withheld |
| `not_applicable` | `idea -> closed`: a REJECT/DROP, not a completion |

The event records the EXPECTATION only, never the outcome — the STATUS commits BEFORE
signing is attempted. A reader combines it with the durable attestation: `required` +
attestation = closed and signed; `required` + none = **signature LOST**; `disposition` +/-
attestation = disposition-signed / disposition-signature-lost; anything else = not expected,
and the value says exactly why.

Precedence: the gate state resolves FIRST (matching `_completion_precheck`'s existing branch
order) — `force_bypassed` is recorded only when the gate was ENABLED and `--force` skipped
it. A forced close under a disabled/unreadable config records `gate_off`/`gate_unreadable`
(no gate to bypass; a FAULT is never masked by a force); the force's reason stays durable in
`force_close_reason` either way.

Computation and threading — NOT `verified_result` (None for force, gate-off, local and
not-certifiable alike, so it conflates the very states this separates):
`_completion_precheck` already visits every branch and now returns the PAIR
`(verified_result, completion_expectation)`; a private in-repo seam — its direct callers and
monkeypatch sites in tests are updated in the same change. `close_ticket` sets
`not_applicable` on the `idea -> closed` branch it already owns and threads the value into
`txn.transition_core`, which gains a keyword parameter and stamps it present-only next to
`close_class` / `force_close_reason` (their exact precedent). Lifecycle-exempt types yield
an empty expectation; their transition is refused before any event is written.

Reduced state: `_fold_close_metadata` (`reducer/_processors_status.py`) folds it on the
winning `*->closed` edge under the same present-only + fork-winner-only rules as
`close_class`; declared as a `$defs` enum in `schemas/common.schema.json`, referenced from
`schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`, `types.py` regenerated. `rebar show` and the MCP
`fetch_ticket` surface it with no further wiring (open dicts).

Backward compatibility (docs/event-schema.md + docs/migrations.md): additive, reducer-known,
present-only. A historical close event lacking the key reduces to state WITHOUT the key —
absent = unknown/legacy, never guessed. No migration; older readers ignore the added key.

Complexity budget: `transition_core` (15) and `_completion_precheck` (15) sit at the ratchet
threshold and `close_ticket` at its frozen ceiling (17); the new logic lands via
behavior-preserving extraction along existing seams — never a baseline bump.

## Scope

* `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py` — return the pair; consume the tri-state; extract
  the gate-resolution head helper
* `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py` — unpack the pair; `not_applicable` on
  `idea -> closed`; thread into `transition_core`
* `src/rebar/_commands/txn.py` — accept and stamp the field on the `*->closed` STATUS event
  in the same locked write (extract the stamping cluster)
* `src/rebar/reducer/_processors_status.py` — fold on both `*->closed` edges
* `src/rebar/schemas/common.schema.json`, `src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json`,
  `src/rebar/types.py` (regenerated) — declare the enum in reduced state
* `docs/event-schema.md` — document the STATUS close-metadata fields incl. the new one
* `tests/unit/test_transition_close.py` (+ existing precheck/reducer test modules whose
  contracts change) — the ACs below

## Testing

Unit tests (happy + failure/edge): one close per enum value read back from REDUCED state;
the three-way signed / signature-lost / gate-off separation; the single-lock assertion via a
counting monkeypatch on `txn._acquire_write_lock`; `gate_unreadable` vs `gate_off`; and the
degrade path — a legacy close event with no key reduces to state with the key ABSENT.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `completion_expectation` is written into the close STATUS event in the SAME locked
      write as the close — verified by a test asserting the write-lock is acquired exactly
      once during a close
- [ ] A later reader, holding no lock and reading only reduced state, separates
      closed-and-signed (`required` + attestation) from closed-with-signature-lost
      (`required`, no attestation) from closed-with-gate-off (`gate_off`) — verified by a
      test closing one ticket each way and asserting all three read back distinctly
- [ ] Each of `force_bypassed`, `local_source` and `not_certifiable` is recorded as ITSELF
      and never as `gate_off` — verified by a test per value
- [ ] An unreadable config records `gate_unreadable`, never `gate_off` (a fault is not
      laundered into a policy choice) — verified by a test
- [ ] A qualifying disposition close records `disposition`, distinct from `required` —
      verified by a test
- [ ] `idea -> closed` records `not_applicable` (a REJECT/DROP is not a completion) —
      verified by a test
- [ ] The expectation is computed independently of `verified_result`, so a `--force` close
      past an ENABLED gate records `force_bypassed`, never gate-off — and a forced close
      under a disabled config records `gate_off` (gate-state precedence, reason still in
      `force_close_reason`) — verified by a test of each
- [ ] The field is documented in `docs/event-schema.md` and is present-only and
      backward-compatible: a legacy close event lacking it reduces to state with the key
      ABSENT (unknown, never guessed) — verified by a test replaying a legacy close event
